landmarks.name: Aïr Mountains
landmarks.writeup: A rugged mountain range in northern Niger known for its unique desert landscapes and prehistoric rock art.

wiki.extract: The Aïr Mountains or Aïr Massif is a triangular massif, located in northern Niger, within the Sahara. Part of the West Saharan montane xeric woodlands ecoregion, they rise to more than 1,800 m (5,900 ft) and extend over 84,000 km2 (32,000 sq mi). Lying in the midst of desert north of the 17th parallel, the Aïr plateau, with an average altitude between 500 and 900 m, forms an island of Sahel climate which supports a wide variety of life, many pastoral and farming communities, and dramatic geological and archaeological sites. There are notable archaeological excavations in the region that illustrate the prehistoric past of this region. The endangered African wild dog once existed in this region, but may now be extirpated due to human population pressures in this region.

landmarks.name: Tenere Desert
landmarks.writeup: Part of the Sahara, famous for its vast sand dunes and the 'Tree of Ténéré,' once considered the most isolated tree on Earth.

wiki.extract: The Ténéré is a desert region in south central Sahara. It comprises a vast plain of sand stretching from northeastern Niger to western Chad, occupying an area of over 400,000 square kilometres (150,000 sq mi). It is bounded by the Aïr Mountains in the west, the Hoggar Mountains in the north, the Djado Plateau in the northeast, the Tibesti Mountains in the east, and the basin of Lake Chad in the south. The central part of the desert contains the Erg of Bilma, an area of sand dunes. The Neolithic Tenerian culture was centred on the region.

landmarks.name: Niamey Grand Mosque
landmarks.writeup: The largest mosque in Niger's capital, an important religious and cultural site.

wiki.extract: The Grand Mosque of Niamey is a Sunni mosque located in Niamey, Niger that was built in the 1970s.

landmarks.name: W National Park
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site shared with Benin and Burkina Faso, known for its biodiversity and wildlife.

wiki.extract: The W National Park or W Regional Park is a major national park in West Africa around a meander in the Niger River shaped like the letter W. The park includes areas of the three countries Niger, Benin and Burkina Faso, and is governed by the three governments. Until 2008, the implementation of a regional management was supported by the EU-funded project ECOPAS. The three national parks operate under the name W Transborder Park. The section of W National Park lying in Benin, measuring over 8,000 km2 (3,100 sq mi), came under the full management of African Parks in June 2020. In Benin, W National Park is contiguous with Pendjari National Park which is also under the management of African Parks.

cultural_events.name: Cure Salée Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual gathering of Tuareg and Wodaabe nomads celebrating the end of the rainy season with music, dance, and camel races.

wiki.extract: The Guérewol is an annual courtship ritual competition among the Wodaabe Fula people of Niger. Young men dressed in elaborate ornamentation and made up in traditional face painting gather in lines to dance and sing, vying for the attentions of marriageable young women. The Guérewol occurs each year as the traditionally nomadic Wodaabe cattle herders gather at the southern edge of the Sahara before dispersing south on their dry season pastures.

food_writeup: Nigerien cuisine features staple foods like millet, sorghum, rice, and maize, often served with sauces made from peanuts, okra, or tomatoes. Popular dishes include 'Djerma' stew and grilled meats.
brief_history: Niger gained independence from France in 1960. It has a history marked by nomadic cultures, colonial rule, and post-independence political changes. The country faces challenges related to development and security.
current_conflicts: Niger faces security challenges from militant groups in the Sahel region, including Boko Haram and ISIS affiliates, impacting stability and development.

commentary.inflation_management: Niger's inflation is anchored by the CFA franc's peg to the euro and has been low for most of the period, with deflation in 2014 (-0.9%), 2019 (-2.5%), and a projected -4.6% in 2025, the series low. The 2008 food crisis pushed it to 10.5%, the series high, and the post-coup sanctions shock to 9.1% in 2024 as borders closed and prices spiked. The BCEAO's regional monetary policy keeps long-run inflation contained, but in Niger prices are driven by rains, uranium markets, and politics; the 2024 spike showed how quickly sanctions can overwhelm the peg's stabilizing effect.
commentary.debt_management: Niger's debt has tripled as a share of GDP on uranium, oil, and security spending. From 14.2% in 2008, the series low, it rose steadily to 51.8% in 2023, the series high, before easing to a projected 45.4% in 2025. The 2023 coup brought ECOWAS sanctions that froze regional market access and central bank assets, forcing domestic financing at higher cost. An oil pipeline to Benin began generating export revenues, improving the outlook, but sustainability depends on sanctions relief and continued market access; the junta's isolation makes both uncertain.

key_events.event: President Tandja's bid to extend his rule triggered a political crisis; military coup followed.
Mahamadou Issoufou won democratic elections; uranium and oil investment grew.
Boko Haram insurgency spread to the Diffa region, raising security spending.
Mohamed Bazoum won the 2021 election, Niger's first democratic transfer.
July 2023: military ousted Bazoum; ECOWAS imposed severe sanctions; Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso formed the Alliance of Sahel States.
With Mali and Burkina Faso, announced ECOWAS withdrawal (early 2024); oil exports via Benin began amid disputes.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The outlook is dominated by politics: uranium and oil give Niger real economic potential, but the junta's break with ECOWAS and Western partners has cut financing and markets. The base case is continued isolation with moderate growth on resource revenues. Upside requires sanctions relief and a political settlement; downside is prolonged isolation pushing debt back up. Uncertainty is very high and entirely political.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
